map.Lessons 6-6, 6-7 & 6-8 — equivalent expr: Lessons 6-6, 6-7 & 6-8. Equivalent expressions. GCF & LCM. The distributive property. The end of the code vault.
map.Previously: the reader dialed the power: Last time: the reader set the power ring right. Exponents beat. Order of operations back. One locked room is left.
map.Previously, in Episode 2: the power ring: Last time, in Episode 2: the power ring spun, locked, and held. Past it waits Ada Vex's last room. The glitch will make its last stand there.
map.Two doors, one lock. Ada's plaque says t: Two doors, one lock. Ada's sign: both faces must show the SAME value. For each number you put in. Only then do they open.
map.Not \"look the same.\" BE the same. x +: Not "look the same." BE the same. Take x + x and 2x. Pick any x you want. Both faces match. Those are real twins.
map.Equivalent expressions name the same val: Equivalent expressions give the same value. It holds for EVERY value of the variable. Twins in new coats.
map.One jacket-swap tool: the distributive p: One coat-swap tool: the distributive property. a(b + c) = ab + ac. The outside number multiplies BOTH terms inside.
map.The glitch slithers across the right-han: The glitch slides across the right door. Plates flicker. Some of these "twins" are… off.
map.It's running a disguise meta — fake twin: It plays a trick. Fake twins match at ONE number. They do not match at the rest.
map.So we test like scientists: feed both fa: So we test like scientists. Put y = 1 in both faces. Then y = 3. One mismatch shows a fake. Or distribute and combine like terms. Terms with the same variable part add up.
map.Algebra unmasks disguises faster than lu: Algebra finds fakes. It is faster than luck. Distribute. Combine like terms. THEN decide.
map.Reader — stamp all four pairs. The glitc: Reader, stamp all four pairs. The glitch needs just ONE wrong stamp. Then the doors stay shut.
map.Four pairs of door-plates glow. Tap a pa: Four pairs of door plates glow. Tap a panel to stamp it. First tap: EQUIV (true twins, equal for EVERY y). Second tap: NOT (a fake). Third tap clears. All four stamps must be right at once.
map.Conceptual: true twins agree for EVERY v: Conceptual: true twins match for EVERY value of y. Put y = 1 in both plates. Then y = 3. One mismatch shows a fake.
map.Procedural: distribute parentheses and c: Procedural: distribute the parentheses. Combine like terms. Then decide. a(b − c) = ab − ac. The multiplier must hit BOTH terms inside. And adding copies is not like multiplying them.
map.I could build this. The link-cog has to: I could build this. The link-cog has to fit BOTH gears. Its tooth count must divide 18 and 30 with nothing left. The biggest one that fits.
map.GCF: the greatest factor two numbers sha: GCF: the greatest factor two numbers share. LCM: the first multiple both counting lists share.
map.And the door-beacons blink every 4 turns: And the door lights blink. One every 4 turns. One every 10 turns. The seal opens the first time they flash TOGETHER.
map.Factors divide IN — a GCF never beats ei: Factors divide IN. A GCF is never more than either number. Multiples count UP. An LCM is never less than either.
map.Reader — cut the link-cog and time the b: Reader, cut the link-cog. Time the lights. Two locks, one hall!
map.Two locks hold the corridor. Cog lock: t: Two locks hold the hall. Cog lock: the cog's tooth count is the GCF of 18 and 30. It is the greatest count that divides both gears. Beacon lock: two lights blink. One blinks every 4 turns. One blinks every 10 turns. They first flash together at their LCM. After how many turns?
map.Conceptual: a GCF divides INTO both numb: Conceptual: a GCF divides INTO both numbers. So it is never bigger than either gear. You count UP TO an LCM. So it is never smaller than either blink number. Factors divide in. Multiples count up.
map.Procedural: list every factor of 18 and: Procedural: list each factor of 18. List each factor of 30. Keep the greatest one both lists share. For the lights, skip-count by 4s and 10s. Stop when both lists reach the same number.
map.The keyway won't take the engraving as w: The key slot won't take the words as written. It wants the factored twin. Put the greatest common factor out front.
map.To expand, push the multiplier through t: To expand, push the multiplier through the parentheses. To factor, pull the GCF back out. Same hall. Walked both ways.
map.Andre's warm-up: 9m + 12. GCF of 9 and 1: Andre's warm-up: 9m + 12. The GCF of 9 and 12 is 3. So it factors to 3(3m + 4). Distribute to check. It snaps right back.
map.Forge the key, reader — GCF out front, n: Make the key, reader! GCF out front. Nothing left to pull!
map.Ada's engraving reads 12x + 30. The keyw: Ada's lock reads 12x + 30. The key slot takes only its factored twin. Put the greatest common factor out front. Leave nothing to pull.
map.Conceptual: factoring runs the distribut: Conceptual: to factor, run the distributive property BACKWARD. Pull the greatest common factor out front. What stays inside must multiply back to the start. Check term by term.
map.Procedural: find the GCF of 12 and 30 fi: Procedural: find the GCF of 12 and 30 first. Then divide EACH term by it. The x-term fills the first blank inside. The constant fills the second. Distribute to check your key.
map.The key turns. And the glitch panics — s: The key turns. The glitch panics. It swells up. It floods BOTH doors at once.
map.Final boss. It's mirroring — one door wa: Final boss. It is a mirror trick. One door wants factoring. The other wants expanding. Both ways at once.
map.And a seal between them demands a REASON: And a seal wants a REASON. Being equivalent is not a feeling. It is a property.
map.Six units of grinding for this moment. R: Six units of work for this moment. Reader, you are my team partner. Let's finish this.
map.If they open, I'm building a replica for: If they open, I'll build one for my room.
map.Boss Gate: factor one door, expand the o: Boss Gate: factor one door. Expand the other. Then stamp WHY your twins must be true.
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. The vault rememb: BOSS GATE. Three locks. The vault knows all you have learned.
map.The glitch floods both doors at once. Th: The glitch floods both doors at once. Three locks. Lock 1: the left door wants the factored twin of 16a + 40. Put the GCF out front. Lock 2: the right door wants the expanded twin: 7(3n + 2). Lock 3: stamp the seal. Say WHY the doors must take your twins.
map.Your two twins are GUARANTEED to match t: Your two twins MUST match the doors' plates. Why?
map.Conceptual: factoring and expanding are: Conceptual: factoring and expanding use the SAME distributive property. They just go opposite ways: a(b + c) = ab + ac. A property makes a sure twin. One lucky number that matches does not.
map.Procedural: Lock 1 — GCF of 16 and 40 fi: Procedural: Lock 1: find the GCF of 16 and 40 first. Then divide each term by it. Lock 2: the multiplier must hit BOTH terms inside the parentheses. Lock 3: pick the reason. It must work for EVERY value of the variable.
Good game. The twin doors had no chance.
map.And THAT — that's Ada's engine room. The: And THAT is Ada's engine room. The whole story starts in there.
map.The cipher vault, the glitch's origin, a: The code vault. Where the glitch came from. The master key. From fraction division to the distributive property. It is all in the main book.
map.Equivalent expressions.Twins name the sa: Equivalent expressions.Twins give the same value. It holds for EVERY value of the variable. One mismatch, at any number, shows a fake.
map.Distributive property.a(b + c) = ab + ac: Distributive property.a(b + c) = ab + ac. The multiplier hits BOTH terms inside. Skip one, and you make a fake. Not a twin.
map.Factor & expand.Expand pushes the multip: Factor & expand.Expand pushes the multiplier through the parentheses. Factor pulls the GCF back out front. Same hall, both ways.
map.GCF & LCM.GCF: greatest factor two numbe: GCF & LCM.GCF: the greatest factor two numbers share. It divides IN. LCM: the first multiple their lists share. It counts UP.
map.\"Two expressions that agree at every nu: "Two expressions may match at each number. Then they are not two things. They are one thing, written twice." — A.V.
map.completed Unit 6 · Episode 3: The Twin D: did Unit 6 · Episode 3: The Twin Doors. You know equivalent expressions. You know GCF & LCM. You can factor with the distributive property.
map.The full story — Vol. 6: The Expression: The full story, Vol. 6: The Expression Engine, waits past the doors.
map.Pair to judge: 4(x + 3) vs 4x + 12. Dist: Pair to check: 4(x + 3) vs 4x + 12. Distribute: 4·x + 4·3 = 4x + 12. The same. True twins.
map.Pair: 3(x − 5) vs 3x − 5. Distribute: 3x: Pair: 3(x − 5) vs 3x − 5. Distribute: 3x − 15. That is NOT 3x − 5. The 3 must multiply the 5 too. A fake.
map.Pair: m + m + m vs 3m. Adding three copi: Pair: m + m + m vs 3m. Add three copies. You get 3 OF them. Twins. MULTIPLYING three copies gives m³. That is a very different thing.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.Different corridor: gears of 12 and 20 t: New hall: gears of 12 and 20 teeth. Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Factors of 20: 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20. Greatest shared factor: 4.
map.Its beacons blink every 3 turns and ever: Its lights blink every 3 turns and every 5 turns. Skip-count: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, … and 5, 10, 15, … The lists first meet at 15. LCM = 15.
map.Sanity rails: a GCF is never bigger than: Quick checks: a GCF is never bigger than either gear. An LCM is never smaller than either blink count. If your answers break these rules, you swapped them.
map.Check by expanding: 3·3m + 3·4 = 9m + 12: Check by expanding: 3·3m + 3·4 = 9m + 12. A true key snaps back to the start.
map.Why guaranteed twins? The distributive p: Why are the twins sure to match? The distributive property holds for EVERY value. So the two forms can not differ. One lucky test is just a clue. The property is proof.
map.Every plate needs a stamp — EQUIV or NOT: Each plate needs a stamp: EQUIV or NOT.
map.5(y+2) = 5y+10 ✓ · 3y+4y = 7y ✓ · 2(y−3): 5(y+2) = 5y+10 ✓. 3y+4y = 7y ✓. 2(y−3) is 2y−6, NOT 2y−3. y·y is y², never 2y. The first seal cracks open!
map.90 is a common MULTIPLE of 18 and 30 — t: 90 is a common MULTIPLE of 18 and 30. The cog wants the greatest common FACTOR. A factor can't be bigger than what it divides.
map.The cog slips. Which tooth counts divide: The cog slips. Which tooth counts divide 18 AND 30 evenly? Take the greatest one.
map.2 is the greatest common FACTOR of 4 and: 2 is the greatest common FACTOR of 4 and 10. The light lock wants their first common MULTIPLE. Count UP, not in.
map.40 is a shared multiple, but the beacons: 40 is a shared multiple. But the lights meet sooner. Think LEAST common multiple.
4 + 10 = 14 is not on either blink list. Skip-count by 4s and by 10s.
map.Beacons still off-beat. Skip-count by 4s: The lights are still off beat. Skip-count by 4s and by 10s. Where do the lists first match?
map.Cog: GCF = 6 teeth. Beacons: LCM = 20 tu: Cog: GCF = 6 teeth. Lights: LCM = 20 turns. KA-CHUNK! The hall seal opens!
map.12x + 30 = 6(2x + 5). The key glows ambe: 12x + 30 = 6(2x + 5). The key glows and turns. The third seal opens!
map.Your key multiplies back to the engravin: Your key multiplies back to the start. But a common factor still hides inside the parentheses. The key slot wants the GREATEST factor out front.
map.The GCF is right! Now divide EACH term b: The GCF is right! Now divide EACH term by it. 12x ÷ 6 gives the x-term. 30 ÷ 6 gives the constant.
map.Start with the GCF of 12 and 30, then di: Start with the GCF of 12 and 30. Then divide each term by it. That fills the parentheses.
map.Lock 1 holds. It multiplies back, but a: Lock 1 holds. It multiplies back. But a common factor still hides inside the parentheses. Pull the GREATEST one out front.
map.Lock 1 holds. The GCF is right! Divide E: Lock 1 holds. The GCF is right! Divide EACH term by it. 16a ÷ 8 gives the a-term. 40 ÷ 8 gives the constant.
map.Lock 1 holds. Start with the GCF of 16 a: Lock 1 holds. Start with the GCF of 16 and 40. Then divide each term by it.
map.Lock 2 holds. The 7 multiplied the 3n bu: Lock 2 holds. The 7 multiplied the 3n. But it skipped the +2. Distribute to BOTH terms.
map.Lock 2 holds. 7 + 3 is not how distribut: Lock 2 holds. 7 + 3 is not how you distribute. The 7 MULTIPLIES each term inside.
map.Lock 2 holds. Push the 7 through the par: Lock 2 holds. Push the 7 through the parentheses. It multiplies the 3n AND the 2.
map.Two locks open! Stamp the seal — choose: Two locks open! Stamp the seal. Pick the reason your twins must be true.
map.Lock 3 holds. One match can be luck — th: Lock 3 holds. One match can be luck. The glitch makes fakes that match at one number. Twins must match at EVERY number.
map.Lock 3 holds. 3(c − 2) and 3c − 2 use th: Lock 3 holds. 3(c − 2) and 3c − 2 use the same numbers. They are NOT twins. Where a number sits changes meaning. Use a property, not a shuffle.
map.Lock 3 holds. Doors judge values, not lo: Lock 3 holds. Doors judge values, not looks. The seal wants a reason. It must work for each value of the variable.
map.16a + 40 = 8(2a + 5) · 7(3n + 2) = 21n +: 16a + 40 = 8(2a + 5) · 7(3n + 2) = 21n + 14 · sealed by the distributive property. THE TWIN DOORS SWING OPEN!
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
